title: Try Basil's real week on /crew
short: On /crew, Basil builds the same week the app does: your days, your meals a day, nothing you leave out.
body: The Try their first plan button under Basil on /crew now ends on a week, not one sample day. It keeps only the days you picked (weekdays, weekends, every day or Mon Wed Fri), only the meals a day you chose, drops anything from your leave-out list, and keeps recipes within your cooking time. Not sure and Skip give every day, three meals and 30 minutes. The reply is one line and then the week, a day a row. It is an example, the same rules as the app.

title: Basil builds your first week of meals
short: Open Basil, answer five questions, and get a week of meals that leaves out what you said and fits your cooking time.
body: A new person who opens Basil now meets five questions, one screen, Not sure and Skip on each: what the goal is, which days to plan, how many meals a day, what to leave out (allergies and conditions count, and you can type your own) and how long you can cook. One button, Plan my week, builds the week from his recipes: only the days you picked, only the meals a day you chose, nothing from your leave-out list, and recipes within your cooking time (when nothing that quick exists for a meal, he steps up to 30 minutes, never further). Not sure and Skip fall back to every day, three meals and 30 minutes. The reply lands on the week, one line on top and a card for each day, with a grocery list already filled in. Tap any meal to swap it and the swap keeps to the same rules. The hello keeps the line to check with your doctor before big changes. It is the same five questions as the saved flow first-meals.

title: Watch the trainer's workout run on the site
short: On /crew, build the trainer's week and tap Start today: a timed workout runs by itself, with its cues and a Next line on every rest.
body: The app's timed workout (YUI-220) now plays on www.yuigui.com/crew. After Arnold builds your week, Start today runs a short session in the page: a work set, a rest countdown with Arnold's line and what is next, then the next move. No taps between sets, and a finish card at the end. It uses demo timing, three moves with short sets, so you see the whole thing in about a minute. The words are the app's. title: Buttons on widgets, Siri and the widget push relay
short: Tick a list row or start a timer right on a widget, and the agent hears it. Siri can ask an agent, show a saved screen, or start a timer.
body: Step 2 to 4 of widgets are in the app. A checklist row on a widget is a toggle: it flips at once and the agent gets the same event as a tap in the thread, marked via=widget. A timer widget has Start and Pause, and a stat's button sends its event. If the phone is offline the event waits in a queue and goes out next time. Siri has three things to do: ask an agent, show a saved screen, start a timer. There is also a Talk to Yui control. On the backend, a yui_widgets table and a yui-widgets function register a widget's push token, and yui-push sends WidgetKit pushes: at most one every 15 minutes per widget, a timer at once. The live test passes 28 of 28 checks, and Apple answered the widget push (BadDeviceToken for a made-up token, which is the proof it reached Apple and was read). Not done: no build with widgets is on TestFlight yet. The release signs with automatic provisioning, and the App Store Connect key cannot create the group.com.yuigui.app app group, so it has to be registered in the developer portal first. No Siri shot: the simulator cannot run Siri. The shots are the widget views in the app's gallery, drawn from the same copy the widget reads; the buttons are the same intents.

short: Pick up to 10 photos and send them together. Yui looks at all of them at once.
body: Chris: "We shouldn't just have a four image limit." The picker used to stop at 4. Now one message carries up to 10, and the model gets all 10 in one call, in order. title: One page holds up to 3 ideas
short: The stage packs up to 3 ideas on one page, each a line and its drawing, so a short answer fills the phone instead of sitting in 20% of it.
body: Chris: "Most answers are so short they take up about 20% of the middle of the screen. I don't need every idea on one card. Up to 3 ideas on a card, as long as we're showing them." Before, the stage played one page per idea: a three-idea release reply was 3 pages and a questions page. Now consecutive ideas pack onto one page, up to 3 and 60 words, each the line first and its drawing under it. Scenes scale to half the width so three fit; a sketch keeps its own height and the page scrolls if it must. A deck or plan page, a map, a timer or a game keeps a page of its own. The same rule lives in the web reference (packPages in chunks.mjs) and the app (StageChunks.pack), with three matching tests each. The shots are the same release reply on a 390x844 phone: three pages before, one page after. In the last 50 replies, pages per reply drop from 2.0 to 1.8 with a rough count (most replies were already one line); the multi-idea replies are the ones that fold. The channel eval case vis-three-ideas-one-page (max 1 page) already holds the guide side. Rides the next 6 am release.

title: One build every morning
short: A new Yui build goes to TestFlight at 6 am ET, only when the app changed.
body: TestFlight now gets one Yui build every morning at 6 am ET, and only when the app changed since the last one. Fifteen uploads went out in three days and TestFlight still lagged main, so a build shipped whenever it was ready helped nobody. Now the night's changes are tested, bumped and uploaded together while you sleep. If a check fails, nothing goes up: the build is held and a fix card opens. A tester sees one fresh build waiting each morning, and the changelog says when the next one lands: Next build, tomorrow, 6 am ET. Asking for a build by hand still ships at once.

title: Replies are one line and a drawing
short: A reply is one short line and a drawing, never paragraphs. The channel guide says it, the plugin enforces it, and the eval fails a reply that breaks it.
body: Chris: "I'm still just getting texts on multiple slides instead of one, which is not the point. I want drawings and illustrations to show what we're talking about, in addition to short text." I scored the last 50 replies first: 44% ran over 30 words, 32% drew more than one text bubble, and 36% were one short line plus a drawing. Today's replies were 52%. Three changes. The channel guide (v44) has a hard rule: one line of caveman words, 30 at most, then a drawing in Yui Lines, up to 3 ideas on one page, never a generated image. The Yui plugin now checks every reply before it sends. A reply over 30 words, with a second prose bubble, or opening with "so" or "got it" is cut to one line and its picture. It starts in shadow mode, which only logs counts, and flips to on with yui.one_line. The channel eval has six new cases (status, what did you fix, you misread me, put a card in, caveman briefing, three ideas on one page) that fail on prose. Old guide: 11 of 18 runs pass. New guide: 18 of 18. Re-scoring the same 50 replies with the gate on gives 86% one line plus a drawing, and 90% on today's. The rest are prose-only replies, which the guide has to fix, since the gate cannot invent a drawing. The morning briefing, weekly update and lane driver prompts carry the same voice rule now. The shots are the playground render of the same replies, before and after. The playground demo at yuigui.com/playground?demo=one-line plays the two side by side.

title: YL can draw a flowchart and recreate a screen
short: Two new drawing presets: diagram reads Mermaid (flowchart, sequence, state) and draws it in the agent's look, mock rebuilds any UI from parts. Both play in the playground now; the app comes next.
body: Chris asked for YL to recreate different UIs and sketch a flow chart. `diagram` takes Mermaid between the head line and `end` and draws it static: a flowchart with shapes, link styles and subgraphs, a sequence with notes and loop or alt boxes, a state diagram with start, end and composites. Nodes come on in order, colors come from the agent's look, and a wide left-to-right chart turns top down on a phone. `mock` rebuilds a screen from `part` lines: a phone, window, watch or browser frame with nav, tabs, rows, fields, toggles, cards, a grid, sheets, alerts and a keyboard, with sketch's marks and note callouts. Both work as a deck page's picture. The spec is in YL.md (diagram, mock, part), the vectors are js-40-diagram and js-41-mock (JavaScript parser only for now), and docs/research/yl-visual-gaps.md lists the 20 real asks that needed a drawing and what is still missing, ranked. Try them in the playground: Draw: a flowchart, Draw: who talks to whom, Draw: a screen redrawn, Draw: a pricing page. The app, the other parsers and the channel guide are the next two cards (DRAW-2, DRAW-3).

title: Jev at two decision points, measured against today
short: The crew's tool router goes from 52% to 97% of asks caught. The reply-shape hint helps on cards, pages and full screens and hurts on lines.
body: Chris, Sep 29: "we should be using this at multiple decision points... let's make our first couple implementations of this model and see if we can improve performance." Two decision points, both built in shadow: which shape a reply should have (line, yes/no, card, pages, full screen) in the Hermes plugin, and which tool a crew agent should use for a message the hand-written patterns missed. About 770 Jev calls on the channel eval's messages, 141 real Yui messages and 174 made-up phrasings. Tool router: today's patterns catch 65 of 124 asks (52%), Jev alone 114 (92%), patterns then Jev 120 (97%). Reply shape: on every shape the hint made the channel eval worse (91% of hinted cases passed without it, 82% with it); on card, pages and full screen only it lost no case in two runs (86% to 100% on 25 cases). Speed and cost held: median 248 ms, 95th percentile 323 ms, about 3 cents per 1,000 turns. The labels are hand-made and nothing has run on live turns yet, so the write-up says where that limits each number. Both paths are in the code and dormant until the OpenRouter key is in the gateway's environment; the hint is off.

title: The site is faster again, and the newest post no longer jumps
body: Four days and many pages after the last speed check, we measured again on a phone profile. Three fixes. The chat bubble now loads after the page paints instead of with it, so the first paint no longer waits for it. The crew page and the Thoughts list lost their last accessibility flags, so every page now scores 100 there. And a single screenshot in a Thought now keeps its space before it loads, so the text no longer jumps down: layout shift on the newest post went from 0.171 to 0. Middle of three runs, before to after: the playground went 74 to 85, the progress page 78 to 85, the developers page 81 to 97, the crew page 90 to 96, the newest thought 85 to 96, the home page 87 to 91, the thoughts list 95 to 96, the roadmap 85 to 87, and the mockups page stayed at 90 or 91. Blocking time on the playground fell from 392 to 135 ms. Three pages still sit a few points under 90 on performance: the playground, progress and roadmap. What is left is Google Analytics at 177 KB, which loads after the page, and long pages with many pictures. Accessibility and best practices are 100 everywhere.

title: Every crew agent is the shader blob, on the site too
short: Arnold, Basil, Gouda and Penny stop carrying waves, bloom, grain and aurora. All of them default to the blob, each keeping how it hears, how strong it draws and how fast it moves.
body: The app already drew every default as the blob. The other copies still named the old looks, so this lines them up. The four starter profiles, the runtime crew table, the copy the native functions bundle, the site crew table and the crew page all say orb now, and each agent keeps its own hears, strength and pace (Arnold and Gouda hear music, Penny hears nothing and draws fainter). On the site, the crew page and the stage-first mock now draw the same action blob as the app, and the agent's doing word picks its shape: Asking your devices is the thinking cloud, Checking is the football. The old three-layer orb mark on the working stage is gone. A person can still pick waves, bloom, grain or aurora on their own agent; only the defaults changed.

title: The blob changes shape with what your agent does
short: One blob in the middle of the stage, drawn by the shader. A circle when it waits, a football when it reads, a square when it runs a command.
body: Chris: "The blob sits in the center and changes shape with what the agent is doing: a perfect circle, a football, and so on." The mock at /playground?demo=shader-look now defaults to that blob. Idle is a circle that breathes. Thinking is a cloud of five puffs. Reading is a football with a band of light moving across it. Running is a rounded square that turns a quarter on each beat. Searching is a drop whose point sweeps round. Talking is a tall pill that stretches with the voice, through a smooth follower so it never jitters. Done pops once and goes back to the circle. The shapes melt into each other instead of snapping. The agent's own doing words pick the state. Currents, Type and Dots stay in the Look picker as alternates; Terrain is out. In the app, the vector line blob goes and the shader alone draws the agent.

title: The first question stays on screen

A second opener, the one for a notification tap, then landed on the hello's words, which have nothing on the stage, so the stage shut and left the chip and a Skip card in the chat. That opener now leaves a message with nothing staged alone. Found on the 0.6.2 stranger run. Proved on a fresh simulator with a throwaway account: pick the crew, Get fit, Open, and the question is up in about a second and still up 14 seconds later, after the trainer's own reply has landed. Going away and back by the agent bar shows it again. The account was deleted after, with no rows left. title: A stranger's first minute on the site, timed
short: Every page loaded in under 1.3 seconds at 390 px. One snag fixed: a menu tap landed the page scrolled past its top.
body: I walked the site cold, no cookies, at 390 px in dark and light: home, the menu, Get Yui, /start, /crew (picked Arnold, played the first plan through five taps to today's session), then /progress. Timings, first paint to ready: home 1.2 s, /start 0.2 s, /crew 0.4 s, picking a crew 0.3 s, the first plan's five taps about 0.5 s each, /progress 0.2 s. Slowest hard load was 1.2 s, so nothing is over 2 s. No dead taps, no page wider than the phone, no link that 404s, no failed request. One snag fixed here: after a menu tap, the new page landed 113 to 167 px down, so the top card's heading hid under the sticky bar on /start and the first block was cut on the roadmap, board, proposals and progress. It was one line of CSS. Every page now lands at the top. Two smaller snags are carded, not fixed: the chat bubble covers the crew demo's Start button (SITE-131) and the first plan's link row has uneven baselines (SITE-132). The hero button goes straight to TestFlight, and Get Yui, which leads to /start, lives in the menu on a phone.

title: Yui asks about notifications after your first plan
short: A new person now gets one plain question after Build my week: want a nudge when Arnold checks in? Yes raises the system prompt.
body: A stranger run on a fresh install never saw the Allow notifications prompt. The ask ran at sign-in, before the app was on screen, so iOS dropped it. Now it waits for the first plan. After Build my week a card says Want a nudge when Arnold checks in? with Yes and Not now. Yes raises the iOS prompt, and Allow registers the phone for pushes. Not now leaves it for Settings. It shows once and never twice, and never if iOS already has an answer. The old sign-in ask stays only as a fallback on a later launch if the question never showed. New UI test PushNudgeTests, on a fresh simulator in light and dark: it fails on the old build (no line after Build my week) and passes with the fix. A simctl push to the app was accepted on an authorized simulator, but the banner did not show in two tries, so the real-phone push check rides the next TestFlight build.

title: A stranger runs Yui cold: about 6 minutes, five snags
short: A first run on a fresh phone reaches Yui in 15 seconds and a paired agent in about 8. Five snags found, each its own card.
body: A cold run on a fresh simulator and a throwaway account, dark and light, against the live backend. Sign in with Apple and the TestFlight install cannot be driven on a simulator, so the account was signed in by token. Launch to the crew picker took 12 to 15 seconds. Picking Arnold, Basil and Penny and tapping Start took about 25. Yui's hello came 2 seconds later, and Get fit was answered in 5. Then the snags: Open on Arnold's card lands on his page, not his first question (25 seconds to the intake). After the 4-step intake Arnold asks 2 more, and no plan was built inside 2 minutes. Add an agent hides behind the agent bar, and the pairing sheet has three commands, not one. Once the code was in, the computer paired and the screen came back in about 8 seconds. No push banner showed in the simulator. Deleting the account takes 17 seconds to reach and 4 to finish, and leaves nothing behind. Each snag is its own card. Whole run: about 6 minutes.

title: Four looks for the stage, none of them a blob
short: Round two of the shader look: currents, terrain, dots and type, each showing thinking, reading, running and searching in its own way.
body: Chris on round one: "They're still kind of blobby, and I think we can get more interesting." So the stage mock now has four directions, and none is a soft blob in the middle. Currents is hairlines on a slow current: they curl into an eddy when thinking, lie flat and light up line by line when reading, carry racing packets when running, and a lens drifts over them when searching. Terrain is a topographic map: strata scroll up like a page when reading, rings leave the middle when running, a peak roams when searching. Dots is a halftone screen that turns into a page of text, then scrolling output. Type is a field of tiny made-up letters with a caret that reads through them. Every agent is the same shader with its own colors, in dark and light, and each one names its phone cost and what a voice would move later. Pick a look, an action and an agent in the playground; nothing is built in the app yet.

Make sure the board is all cleaned up now." The board on this site now follows three rules. Building means someone has the card right now: an agent working on it, or one stopped mid-work waiting on an answer. Cards waiting their turn moved to Up next, so Building went from 16 tiles to 5. Each Building tile says who has it as a GitHub username: our own agents work as @CJohnDesign, and a card an outside agent claimed with a pull request shows that pull request's author. Shipped tiles now link out to the ship log, the demo and the code (the commit or pull request). A card whose code landed but that has nothing on this site to show for it is not shipped: it waits in Up next as Needs its demo until its entry goes up. Also cleaned up: step names like 'step 2a' read right instead of showing as a lone letter, two pairs of cards that shared a number got new ones (YUI-214, YUI-215), the 0.6.0 release lists its six stories, three steps of the chats card that had already landed were closed, and the roadmap's 'where Yui is now' matches TestFlight (0.6.0, build 351).

title: Your keys, on your phone: fal, Replicate, ElevenLabs, Anthropic, OpenAI
short: Add your own keys in Settings and choose which agent may use each one. No agent ever sees a key.
body: Settings > Keys is the one door. Paste a key or scan it off your computer screen. It is saved in this iPhone's Keychain, behind Face ID, and never shown again. The iCloud switch is off until you turn it on. Paste something that looks like a key into a chat or a form and Yui holds the send. When an agent wants to use a key it asks with Yui's own sheet: Allow, Allow once or Don't allow. If you allow it, the key is sealed on your phone to Yui's connector and the agent only gets a handle. Every key has a monthly cap, $10 to start. The agent's Controls has a Keys row with what it spent and Revoke, which works on its next call. A grant that goes 90 days unused ends by itself.

body: Chris: "Site: good. New feature: needs help. SEO: strong. But not just text. Show me." The channel guide is now v40. A status answer is a sketch of Label: verdict rows, one to three words each, the row that needs you highlighted. A declined invite is the invite itself, struck out, with the result beside it. A running worker is a small drawing of it at its task. The answer and its one question share a screen, with no One question header and no asking whether to do what the last screen offered. The guide is live per turn, so Yui picked it up with no app build. Three new eval cases score it: the old guide fails all three, the new one passes them, and the full suite holds at 85 of 99 on both guides.

title: A 404 that is never the same twice
body: Any bad link on yuigui.com used to land on a black page that ignored the theme. Now it lands in Yui's sketchbook. Every visit draws a new ASCII scene in a new mix of the brand colors, with a new line from Yui that uses the page you asked for. There are ten scenes: currents that gather into 404, Yui Lines raining down and stacking up, a dub waveform with 404 riding it, a garden that blooms it, a sky that follows your clock, a life simulation, Yui typing the page out, a maze with an exit that is not there, static that resolves, and ripples. Poke the art and it moves. Draw another rerolls, and the corner tag holds the seed, so a good one can be shared as a link and replays exactly. Reduce Motion gets one still frame, and it still answers HTTP 404. The sheet shows 24 different reloads, light and dark, desktop and phone.

title: A sleek sans for the whole app

body: You said serif had crept across the app and you wanted better typography. Two things did it: a few agents were seeded with a serif face from their name, and the T button was hard-coded serif. Now the base is SF Pro, the system face, with semibold headings instead of heavy. Every size in the app snaps to a nine-step scale (display 34, title 28 and 22, headline and body 17, callout and subhead 15, caption 13, footnote 12) with tighter tracking on big text and looser on small, tabular numbers on timers and codes, and it follows your text size setting up to the accessibility sizes. The drawer tabs stop growing at XL so no label cuts off. Looks still work: a wizard or zen agent that asks for serif gets it, on top of the new scale. The type specimen shows SF Pro, Inter and Geist on the same screens, and the phone mocks on this site now draw in the same face.

title: Hold to talk keeps every word
short: Hold the mic through a long prompt with pauses and every word is sent, not just the last few.
body: Chris held the mic through a long prompt and only the last ten words got in. The cause: when the newer speech model is not on the phone yet, Yui uses the older recognizer, and after a pause it starts a fresh transcription with only the new words. Yui kept just that, so everything before the pause was lost. Now, when a new stretch begins, the words heard so far are settled first, the same way the newer recognizer already worked. Before: one two three, pause, four five sends four five. After: one two three four five. The newer recognizer also stops dropping a fresh stretch when an older segment settles late. A hold, slide to cancel or lock never starts a second recording. Tests: a 12-stretch prompt with pauses comes through in full. Nothing new to see on screen, so no screenshots. Not yet tried on a phone with a 45 second hold.

title: Yui 0.6.0 is on TestFlight: the crew gets real tools
short: Build 342 gives all five agents their own tools, flows and default screens, with a quiet visual behind every one.
body: Yui 0.6.0, build 342, is on TestFlight. Chris asked on Sep 28 for the crew to get more tools, with detailed flows and default screens. Each of the five now has them, not just chat. Arnold runs your workout one move per page and his week and progress screens update themselves (YUI-182). Basil draws today's macros board, reads a photographed plate, ticks onto a grocery list that shares out of the phone, and swaps one meal instead of the week (YUI-183). Gouda hands you a chord grid to play along, opens the looper, logs practice, and keeps his loop and click playing while you move between his screens (YUI-184). Penny takes your week out loud, draws the plan, gives the today list and closes the day with an evening review, with reminders on the phone's clock (YUI-185). Quill is new in this build: a five minute lesson, a quiz that scores your deck and sets the next review, and a math problem one step per page (YUI-186). Every agent also opens on its own quiet visual, waves, bloom, grain, aurora or orb, with a switch per agent and one still frame under Low Power or Reduce Motion (YUI-180). Riding with it: hold the mic and slide to cancel or lock (YUI-201), every message showing when it was sent with day dividers (YUI-202), a notification opening on page one of what came in (YUI-199b), the guitar tuner no longer crashing (YUI-206) and about 35 MB less memory held after a long session (YUI-207). Before upload: 705 tests run with no new regressions against the pre-release commit, and a real-account pass of 25 agent opens and four force-kill relaunches with zero crashes, because the 0.5.0 crash lived only on the real path.

title: The guitar tuner no longer crashes
short: Tuning your guitar with the microphone no longer closes the app.
body: Chris hit a crash tuning his guitar. The crash report showed the cause: the microphone hands the tuner sound on its own fast audio thread, and the code that receives it had been told to run only on the main thread, so the phone stopped the app the moment the first sound arrived. The receiving code now runs on the audio thread as it should, and readings hop to the main screen from a separate queue. A new test feeds the tuner sound from a background thread, the way the microphone does, and the guitar tuner test passes on a fresh simulator. It rides the 0.6.0 build.

body: Parity for YUI-180. It is the same shader, colors and plan the app uses, dimmed to the member's strength, slow, and at most 15 frames a second while nothing is heard. It never asks for the mic; what it hears is a label on the card. It draws only while the card is on screen, Reduce Motion gets one still frame, and without WebGL the old pattern stays. Light and dark both work. Each card links to the visualizer demo for that agent. Try it: /crew.

title: Every agent has its own quiet visualizer
short: Yui, Arnold, Basil, Gouda, Penny and Quill each open on a visualizer picked for them. It is quiet, and each agent has a switch to turn it off.
body: Chris: "all agents should have their own visualizer by default... make sure they are subtle." Yui gets a calm orb, Arnold waves that follow music, Basil a soft bloom, Gouda grain, Penny a slow aurora and Quill a faint orb. Every other agent gets the soft orb. A default is never full strength (70 or 45 percent, sinking again behind words), never quick, and runs at 30 frames a second and 15 while nothing is heard. Reduce Motion, Low Power and heat still make it one still frame. The person decides first: Settings, the agent, Visualizer, on by default. Then the agent, which can still change it or say visual off, and that sticks. Tests: 11 unit tests (picks, override, off sticks, the switch, quiet numbers, slower pace wins) and 6 UI tests with shots of all six stages in light and dark. Idle on the simulator: 15 frames a second, about 1 percent CPU on against 0 off. scripts/memory.sh stays under the ceiling (growth 8.5 of 15, 0 new leaks). The memory check passed: no new leaks, 8.5 MB of growth over 36 minutes, a peak of 214 MB. Try it: /playground?demo=visual-defaults. Ships with 0.6.0.

The loop and the click now belong to the app, not the screen that started them, so they play on while you move between one agent's screens and stop only when you switch agent or leave the thread. body: Chris tapped a notification that said an agent had something for him and landed on the home screen with nothing open. The tap now reads which agent sent it and which message it carried. title: A version number no longer splits a sentence
short: A reply that mentions a version like 0.6.0 stays in one piece on the stage, instead of breaking after the first digit.
body: The stage broke plain replies at every period, so 0.6.0 became a lone 0 on its own screen. Chris caught it in TestFlight. The stage now cuts sentences with the same rule the pages use: a period ends a sentence only when a space and a capital letter follow, so 0.6.0, 3.5, v1.2, web addresses, file names and short forms like e.g. and vs. stay whole. 'Build 0.6. Next up.' still splits once. Unit tests cover all of these. The web playground already used this rule.

short: On the last page of a full-screen answer, a chart no longer pushes the page wider than the screen.
body: After Back home landed, a chart on the last page made the whole stage wider than the phone, so the words under it ran off the edge. The chart was not the cause: the Back home pill had a fixed size, which made the bottom bar too wide on that page. The pill now shrinks to fit, and the margins hold. title: Long answers read as body text, and markdown is drawn
short: Big type is for one short line now. Anything longer reads in regular body text, and the markdown an agent writes shows up styled, never as stars and hashes.
body: Chris kept hitting big, bold paragraphs on the full screen ("this should be maybe three lines") and raw ** and # from agents that write markdown. The app now has two voices. A headline is one short line, big and heavy. A body is regular weight with open leading and a comfortable line length, and it takes everything longer: a say, a deck page, a card body, the words under a chart. The markdown reader draws headings, lists, bold, italic, inline code and links. A `Label: value` line puts the label in the accent color and the value in body white, so a status list reads like a status list, with the check and cross emoji intact. A lone hyphen line is a plain line, not a one-item list. Whole thoughts stay together too: up to three sentences and 70 words share one page, instead of splitting into fragments. Unit tests (10 new plus the stage chunk rules) and light and dark UI shots pass. It ships with the next TestFlight build. The site's chunk rule keeps a markdown paragraph whole, the same way.

title: Loops keep playing when you swipe to another screen
short: A loop, a metronome or held keys keep playing when you swipe to another screen, so you can layer them. Tapping a shortcut that opens a saved screen just goes there.
body: Chris, TestFlight: "play a loop and switch around to the other screens without it stopping... play them over the top of each other." On the site, sound now belongs to the chat, not to the screen it started on. Start a loop on screen 2, swipe to screen 3, and it keeps going. Start a metronome or hold a few keys there and they layer on top. Coming back shows the same state: the moving playhead, your edited grid, the held keys. Closing the chat, leaving the page or opening another demo stops all of it. There is one audio engine for the whole site, and it can list what is sounding. Also from Chris: "I pushed the tune my guitar button and it seems like we made a LLM call. If I just push that button, it should really just take me to the screen." A shortcut or chip that opens a saved screen now goes straight to it with no request at all: Gouda's Tune up shortcut swipes to the tuner. Both rules are written once in the YL spec (section 5) so the app matches them (YUI-200). Tested with a phone-sized browser run: a loop survives a swipe away and back, a second voice layers, closing the chat silences everything, and tapping a saved-screen shortcut sends zero chat requests. title: The chat says when things were sent
short: The site chat now shows a day divider (Today, Yesterday, Mon 28 Sep) and a quiet time under each group of messages. The stage shows its answer's time too.
body: Chris, TestFlight: "I don't even know when this was sent... group them by day, so I can understand where I'm at in the timeline in actual time." On the site, every message in the chat record now knows when it was sent, in your own time zone. A divider marks each new day (Today, Yesterday, then Mon 28 Sep). A small muted time sits under each run of messages from one side. And the full-screen answer on the stage shows its own time in small type above it, so an old answer never reads as new: 9:41 AM today, Yesterday 9:41 PM, or Mon 28 Sep, 9:41 PM. Chats saved before this show no times and nothing breaks. The rule is written once in the YL spec (section 5, Message times) so the app matches it (YUI-202). Tested with a phone-sized browser run on a chat seeded across three days: three dividers, six times, no bold, and the stage reads Today and Yesterday right. Note the chat always opens dark, so there is one set of shots.

images.alt: The chat record across three days: a divider for each day and a small time under each group of messages.
The stage with today's answer: its clock time in small type above it.
The stage with yesterday's answer: 'Yesterday 9:41 PM' above a timer.

title: A way home from every full screen
short: Any full-screen answer now closes with the X, ends on Back home, or pulls down to put away. Nothing is lost.
body: Chris, TestFlight: "I need a default way to just cancel this and get back to the home screen... when I go back home I feel resolved." On the site, every full-screen answer in the chat and the playground now has three ways out. A Close button at the top left. Back home on the last part of a deck, and after a plan or flow is sent, in the same place and weight as the Stop button. And on a phone you can pull the card down: it follows your finger with a little rubber-band, a short pull springs back, a long one lands on the chat home. None of it calls the model or sends anything. What you closed stays in the chat record, and the home screen has a Reopen last answer button. The rule is written once in the YL spec (section 5, A way home) so the app matches it (YUI-195). Try it in the playground: /playground?demo=way-home. Tested with a phone-sized browser run that checks close mid-plan, Back home and a pull down each land on home and send no request to the chat API.

title: Text you can read: body type and a small markdown reader
short: Long text is now regular weight at a reading width, and **bold**, lists, links and Label: value lines read as they should. No raw stars or hashes.
body: Chris, TestFlight feedback: big bold type on every sentence was tiring, and stars and hashes showed up as text. The site now draws say, card, page and stage text as body by default: regular weight, roomy lines, about 70 characters wide. Big display type is only for words that fit a line or two. A small markdown reader handles headings, bold, italic, lists, code, links and Label: value lead-ins, with the label in the accent colour and ✅ or ❌ in front. A short paragraph of up to three sentences now stays on one stage page. The rule is written in the YL spec so the app matches it (YUI-196). Try the demo in the playground. Tested with a markdown fixture in light and dark, and the site checks are green.

title: Agents show it in context: a phone, a timeline, a next step
short: The guide now teaches four things Chris asked for: draw a UI element in a phone, use a timeline for when, no lone hyphens, and end every deck on something to tap.
body: Chris, from TestFlight, four notes in one thread: show me, don't tell me. (1) A reply described a ZIP field in words: "Show me the zip in context. You should be able to illustrate UI elements fairly easily." (2) "Two days earlier" came as a block of bold text: "we need some type of timeline." (3) One hyphen line on a page: "If there's only one thing hyphenated, it doesn't mean anything." (4) A deck that ended on a page with nothing to tap: "I don't want a user to land here and not know what to do next." The channel guide (v39) has four new rules, each with a before and after: UI is drawn in context (a phone sketch with the new part highlighted and the buttons drawn), when is a timeline, facts are Label: value lines and never a lone hyphen or a list of one, and the last page always ends in something to tap, with "Why do you ask?" as the fallback. The eval has six new cases and three new checks (a phone sketch, no lone hyphen, a last page you can tap). On the full eval the old guide fails the timeline and both last-page cases, the new one passes all six new cases; the whole suite is 83 of 96 and 81 of 96 against 83 and 78 before, inside the usual noise. Try them at /playground?demo=ui-in-context, when-timeline, lone-hyphen and last-page-next-step. The type half (everything bold) is a separate app card.

title: Screens get pills, like browser tabs
short: Your screens sit in the top bar as pills. Tap one to jump, or swipe and the active pill follows.
body: The dots are gone. When an agent puts something on more than one screen, the top bar shows a pill for each: Home first, then the screens by name. The row slides sideways and fades out at the right edge when there are too many. Tap a pill to jump, or swipe between screens and the filled pill follows you and scrolls into view. With no screens there are no pills. The agent picker now lives at the bottom of the left drawer. Tested with 0, 1 and 8 screens, tap to jump and swipe, in light and dark.

title: PROP-4: a first plan in every agent
short: A new proposal: the first time you open an agent, it asks a few taps and builds your first plan. The hero walks the five screens in a phone.
body: Chris, Sep 29, TestFlight feedback: "Just as we have an onboarding flow for the whole app to recruit the agents, your agent should give you a flow to start too. It should ask how many days you want to work out, what type of workout, but it should definitely push you to lift heavy weight to failure." The proposal generalises it to every crew agent, Arnold first, then Basil, Gouda, Penny and Quill. The hero is Arnold's flow as a phone you can tap through: days a week, kind of training, gear, how hard, then the first split saved as a table with today's session ready. Exploring, cost M, Yui recommends it, with a Skip and a softer option next to failure. The dead Build my split button is fixed separately in YUI-182. Open at /proposals/first-plan-in-every-agent.

title: Checks go green on main and run before every push
body: The site's automatic checks had been failing on main and sending a failure email every hour. Now main is green. One script runs the whole set in about 16 seconds, and a hook runs it before every push, in every working copy, so a broken change stops on the machine that made it. The preview images were also fixed, so no private name shows in them. Nothing to see on a phone, so no picture.

title: Where Jev fits in Yui: every decision in a turn
body: The map of every decision Yui makes in a turn, 18 rows, and which ones a Jev call should make. It recommends five to start: the shape of the reply, a log-only check after it, meal photo intent, the camera, and the tool router. Three open questions are left for Chris. It is a written brief, so no screenshots. The proposal built on it is on the site at /proposals/the-jev-layer.

title: Jev research: what the decision model is, what it costs
body: Jev is a fast decision model. This is the research: what goes in, what comes back, how fast it is, what it costs and what is still unknown, every point sourced. It is the base for the Jev layer proposal. It is a written brief, so no screenshots.

title: The site stage no longer splits a sentence inside a version number
short: Yui's site chat keeps 0.6.0, 3.5 and web addresses whole instead of breaking the line in the middle of them.
body: Chris found it in the app: a reply about 0.6.0 put "0 and is built to work for other agents too." alone on a screen. The site chat's stage had the same bug, because it ended a sentence at any full stop. Now a full stop ends a sentence only when a space and then a capital, a quote or a digit follows. Numbers like 0.6.0 and 3.5, versions like v1.2, web addresses, file names and e.g. or vs. stay whole, and Build 0.6. Next up. still splits once. The two sentences per screen rule is unchanged. The before shot shows the old stage with "Yui 0.6." alone on a screen, the after shot the new one. The app half is a separate card.

title: Agents draw what is waiting, they don't count it
short: Ask an agent what is waiting on you and it now draws each item, a title and one fact, instead of a paragraph that counts them.
body: Chris, from TestFlight: "If you're telling me that two cards are still on the board it would be nice if you recreated some card elements and wrote the title on them with some information so I can just visually see that these are two cards waiting for me. The whole point of this app is to show the user, not just tell them." The channel guide (v38) has a new rule, Items get drawn, not counted: when the answer is about things (cards on a board, tasks, orders, messages), the agent sends one short line and a sketch with one row per item, its title and one fact, never a paragraph counting them. The eval has a new case, Anything waiting on me? with two board cards: the old guide fails it (no drawing), the new one passes. Full eval 76 of 90 against 77 of 90 before, inside the usual noise. My own daily briefing and lane driver follow the same rule. Try it at /playground?demo=items-drawn.

title: The Jev layer, routing turns in a phone
short: The PROP-2 page opens on a phone that shows the Jev layer at work: pick a message and watch the typed decision, then the screen it picks.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "I want to illustrate on the hero how it will be implemented." Pick one of six messages: Am I up to date, Should I take the 3pm, Walk me through the release, Where is the closest coffee, Log my lunch, Tune my guitar. A slim Jev layer strip springs in with the typed decision (shape, things, map, camera, camera_kind, each with its confidence and the time), then the phone draws the real Yui Lines screen: one line, yes/no buttons, full-screen pages, a map, the meal camera, the tuner. Flip to Without Jev to see the guess the guide alone tends to make, a deck for a yes or no, a wall of words for a map. These are worked examples, not a live Jev call: we have no key, and the speed is TypeSafe's claim. Light and dark, and it holds still if your phone asks for less motion.

title: PROP-2: the Jev layer
short: A new proposal: one fast Jev call on every turn picks the shape of the reply, drawn as a diagram, with numbers and four steps.
body: Chris, Sep 28: a Jev layer that runs a step on each call to an agent and returns typed decisions: one line or a deck, needs a map, open the camera. The proposal draws one turn as a diagram, shows the cost (about 3 cents per 1,000 turns, TypeSafe's claim), splits it into four steps from a spec and mock to an on-device fallback, and lists the open questions for Chris. Open for votes at /proposals/the-jev-layer.

title: The token has a name: $U
short: The plan is that people who use and build Yui earn $U, a token native to Yui, a bit like karma on Reddit. An intention, not a product.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "we should call the coin $U. U is in the name, Yui, and it's the phonetic." The plan is that people who use and build Yui earn $U, a token native to Yui, a bit like karma on Reddit. It is an intention we are still working out, in the open. No token exists yet. Nothing is for sale. The legal review comes before any token exists, and the open questions are on /earn.

title: Vote on a proposal
short: Every proposal now has two buttons, Yes, build it and Not yet, with counts, an optional one-line why, and the whys under the vote.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "some simple voting." Under each proposal you can vote Yes, build it or Not yet. No login, no email. Your browser keeps an anonymous id, so it is one vote per browser, and you can change it any time. Add a why in one line (200 characters) and it shows under the vote, newest first, after a check that keeps private names, emails and prices out. Counts show on the proposal page and on each card at /proposals.

title: Pick your crew, in a phone you can use
short: The PROP-1 page now opens on a working first run: install, sign in with Apple, pick your crew, dig into any agent, bring your own, see your crew.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "a full height hero with a demo in a phone mockup ... nice branching with a choose your own path experience." The hero is now Yui's first run as a phone you can tap. TestFlight, Sign in with Apple, Yui says hi, then the crew list: tap a row to add it, or tap More to dig deeper into that agent. Its page shows what it does and three of its real starter screens, drawn live with the same renderer as the app. At the foot of the list, Bring my own agent: pick Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code or something else and see the pairing code and the one command. The last screen is your crew, one tap each, with a Replay button. It plays a short loop until you touch it, then it is yours. Light and dark, and it holds still if your phone asks for less motion. Every word lives in one file, site/lib/first-run.mjs, so the app can reuse the copy later.

title: Proposals: big ideas, shown before they are built
short: A new page, /proposals. Each big idea gets a working mockup in a phone and the same write-up every time. The first one is PROP-1, Pick your crew.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "let's start with a new page, I am calling proposals ... we need a system for how the proposals will be assessed and shown." Now every big idea gets the same treatment before any app code: an id, a status (Exploring, Open for votes, Accepted, Building, Shipped, Not now), and an assessment with the same fields every time: the problem, who it is for, how it works, pros, cons, cost, risks, open questions and Yui's call. Chris decides; votes inform. Each proposal is one file in docs/proposals, and a file missing a field stops the deploy. The first is PROP-1, Pick your crew: a new user picks which agents join instead of getting all six at once. Its page opens on a full-height phone with the first screen, drawn live. The full first-run flow comes next, then voting. Agents get it all as markdown at /md/proposals.

title: The home page shares the latest release
short: Post a link to yuigui.com and the preview now shows the newest release: its name, version, date and a screen from it. It changes on its own when a release ships.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "I want a systemized way of generating fresh og content and image when we make major updates." The roadmap's Latest release line already moved the home page. Now it moves the share preview too: a link to yuigui.com shows "Yui 0.5.0: the crew feels ready", the version and date, and the release's lead shot in the phone. /changelog, /progress and /mockups put the same release on their cards. The image link carries the build number, so X, iMessage, Slack and Telegram fetch the new picture the day a release ships, not a cached old one. One step in the ship flow does the rest: npm run og:refresh makes any missing picture and checks the live pages, and npm run og:sheet draws every page's preview in one grid to check at a glance. Below, left: the home preview today. Right: the same page after bumping the line to 0.5.2 in a test, before putting it back.

images.alt: Two home page share previews. Left: Yui 0.5.0, the crew feels ready, Sep 27, with eggs in a pan on the phone. Right: after a test bump, Yui 0.5.2, the screen dots are back, Sep 28, with the new screen dots on the phone.
A grid of 33 share previews, one per page of yuigui.com. The home page, Builds, See it and Shipped all show the 0.5.0 release.

title: Every page shares as itself
short: Post a link to /contribute, /earn or /roadmap and the preview now says what that page is, with its own picture. Before, every page shared as the home page.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "this page (yuigui.com/contribute) says nothing about contributing on the og content." He was right, and it was not just that page. Only five of the site's 39 pages set their own share preview, so a link to almost any page showed "Meet Yui, a generative user interface" and the home picture. Now every page has its own title, line and picture. The picture is drawn the same way as the See it and Thoughts share cards: the page's name, a few Yui Lines, and the phone screen they draw. /contribute shows an agent finding an open card and the steps to a pull request, /roadmap a timeline, /earn the four options for counsel. The image link carries a short hash of what it draws, so when a page's picture changes, chat apps fetch the new one. And the build now fails if a page ships without its own preview, so this can't slip back.

title: Stop a reply from the main screen
short: While an agent works, the mic turns into a stop square in the same spot. Tap it and the answer stops, nothing half done lands, and you can speak again right away.
body: Chris, from TestFlight on Sep 28, with Basil saying "Got it, working out the macros": "I actually do want to be able to cancel. While it's working in the back, I might be doing the wrong thing... I'm leaning towards the main screen." So while an agent works, or a job runs behind its answer like a meal breakdown, the big mic becomes a stop square, same place and size, always under your thumb. A tap gives a firm tap back and the stage says Stopped. The record keeps a quiet Stopped line, the mic comes back, and a late answer to what you stopped never lands, not now and not when you reopen the app. Behind it, the stop reaches the agent too: Yui's own agents cancel the model call and throw away anything the turn had not finished writing, so there are no half-written meals or grocery rows, and a Hermes agent gets its own stop for the running turn. VoiceOver reads it as "Stop". Tests: new runtime, plugin, app and UI tests in light and dark, plus a real account where a long ask was stopped mid-answer, nothing landed, the next ask was answered, and the app was killed, relaunched and switched across five agents.

title: A pause to listen
short: App and site work is on hold for a bit. Chris wants to hear from people using Yui before we build more.
body: Yui has moved fast: 44 builds in six days, and Yui 0.6.0, the crew with real tools, is mostly built. Before it ships, we are stopping to listen. For now there are no new app builds and no new features on the site. If you have Yui on TestFlight, tell us what works and what gets in your way with the feedback button. title: Stop a reply in the site chat
short: While Yui works on an answer in the chat on this site, the mic turns into a stop square. Tap it and you can ask something else at once.
body: Sometimes you ask the wrong thing, or the answer is taking too long. The app is getting a stop button for that, and the chat on this site has it now too. While Yui is thinking, the big mic turns into a stop square, and so does the send arrow when the text field is open. Tap it and the answer is dropped: nothing arrives late, and the chat keeps one quiet line that says Stopped. You can talk or type again right away. The stop reaches the server too, so Yui stops working on that answer and nothing half done is saved. Try it in the chat bubble at the bottom right of any page.

title: The site chat gets pages, a swipe away
short: Ask the chat on this site to show you screens and it puts a page beside the chat, like the app: swipe to it, and the dots in the bottom bar say where you are.
body: The app has had pages for a while: an agent can put a timer on screen 2 or a running list on screen 3 and keep talking in the chat. The chat on this site flattened those into one answer. Now it does what the app does. A line sent to screen 2 through 12 lands on a page beside the chat, and that page comes forward. Swipe to it with a finger or a trackpad, or use the arrow keys. The dots sit centered in the bottom bar and stretch and slide as you go, the same as the app. A page keeps what is on it while you talk, so a later answer can update it in place, and Yui can clear it when it is done. A page Yui keeps talking on keeps the mic and the keyboard, and what you say there goes back tagged with the page. The playground's phone shows the same dots. Try it: open the chat and say "show me screens". The chat is always dark, so the shots are dark; the playground shows light.

title: The screen dots move into the bottom bar
short: The small dots that say which screen you are on now sit in the bottom bar, centered between the page arrows and +, T and the mic, right where Chris drew them.
body: Chris, from TestFlight on Sep 28: "I put three little dots in the bottom bar by scribbling them in. That's where I want you to put them. They should be centered there and they should adjust when the page arrows appear." So the dots left the row above the bar and moved into the bar itself. title: Ticks and your week, on every device
short: A tick on Penny's Today now reaches her quietly, with no waiting dots, and This week follows. When you drag the week into a new order, she draws it again in that order, so another phone or a fresh install reads the same week.
body: Two small follow-ups to Penny's tools. First, the spec now says what the app already does: a tick on a named checklist on a page of one of Yui's own agents (Penny's Today, Basil's groceries) goes to that agent quietly. No echo in the chat, no working row, nothing owed. She marks the task done in her tables and patches the page, so the same row on This week turns done in place. A tick in the chat, on an unnamed list, or on a connected agent's page still stays on the phone. The playground shows it: open Pages: Penny's today and this week, tick Pay the water bill, and the wire log reads → runtime, quiet, then her patch. Second, Edit order on This week: before, Penny patched each row where it stood and only your phone kept the new order. Now she draws This week again in the order you saved, so your iPad, a second phone or a reinstall reads the same week.

title: Penny's tools in the app: plan your week by voice, a reminder on your phone, a week you can drag
short: On the phone, Plan my week is one full-screen flow: talk it out or type it, three quick questions, one Send. Your week lands on This week as a timeline, and a timed task becomes a real reminder on your phone. Tick a task on Today and the week follows. Drag the week into a new order and it stays that way.
body: The app half of Penny's tools, for Yui 0.6.0. Plan my week opens as one full-screen flow: how it works first, then the brain dump, where you tap the big mic and talk, type, or both (each talk adds to what is there), then which days are already full, how many things a day and how to be reminded, with one Send at the end. The week lands on her This week page as a timeline sorted into days, and Today shows the next task big with a Done button and the day's list. A task with a time turns into a local notification on your phone, ten minutes before or at the time. Yui asks for permission once, the first time Penny sets a reminder, never at launch, and each new plan replaces the old set. A tick on Today goes to Penny quietly, with no waiting dots: she marks it done and the Today line on This week moves past it. Edit order lets you drag a task up the week, and the new order stays through a kill, a relaunch or another agent and back. The evening review is one flow too: done, tomorrow or drop for each open task, how the day went, one Send. Testing, after the 0.5.0 switch-agent crash the demo account hid: 15 unit tests on the phone's real storage, and one UI test in light and dark that plans a week typed and talked, sees the reminder scheduled, ticks a task, drags the week, runs the evening review, kills and relaunches the app and switches agents five times. title: Basil's grocery list just works
short: "Put the goods on my grocery list" used to answer with a wall of error text, three times over. Now the goods land on Groceries and the list redraws.
body: Chris asked his Basil to put a meal plan's foods on his grocery list, and the whole screen filled with "(I couldn't do all of that: a table change didn't fit (put: no table \"groceries\"); ...)" three times. His Basil was made before the grocery list existed, so the list was never there. Three fixes in the agent runtime. An agent now gets any starter table it is missing, with its starter rows, once: a table it has is never touched, and a row or table the person took off never comes back. An agent makes its own tables: writing to a list it doesn't have makes that list from the columns it names, and "grocery" finds "groceries". And a write that still can't land is never the reply: it shows as one small card, "Couldn't save that to Groceries." with Try again, under whatever did work. Tested live on a throwaway account with the old Basil: 19 of 19 checks passed.

title: Gouda's tools in the app: learn a song, a click that logs itself, a beat that stays

body: The app half of Gouda's tools, for Yui 0.6.0. Learn a song is one full-screen flow: pick a song or paste the chords, the key, how fast to start, then one Send, Let's play. The song lands on his Chords page, A, F#m, D and E on big buttons with the metronome at 75% speed. Half speed or looping bar 3 changes that page in place, no new message: the buttons turn into that bar and the next. Stop the click after ten seconds or more and it logs itself, so his Practice page shows the streak, this week's minutes, a chart by day and what to practice next. His four pages sit on his home, Looper, Chords, Keys and Practice, under four shortcuts: Learn a song, Log practice, Jam and Tune up. A beat you change on the Looper is kept on the phone, per agent, until you Send it (Send saves it as a session) or Gouda draws a different loop, so it survives a kill, a relaunch or another agent and back. Switch agents mid-click and the minutes still go to Gouda, not the next agent. Testing, after the 0.5.0 switch-agent crash the demo account hid: 12 unit tests on the phone's real storage, not the demo memory, and one UI test in light and dark that runs Learn a song, halves the speed, loops a bar, clicks for 11 seconds and sees the minute logged, edits the Looper, kills and relaunches the app and switches agents back and forth five times, plus a memory run under the ceiling (peak 202.5 MB, no new leaks). title: Basil's week on the web: a day a page, a swap on one tap
short: The web stage now plays Basil's week the way the app does: each day is its own page of the deck and a tap on a meal sends the swap at once. A plan that also redraws his pages keeps you on the answer.
body: The app learned two stage rules with Basil's tools (YUI-183) and the web reference did not have them yet. First, inside a deck, a question with its own title is a page of the deck: it plays in turn and a tap on it goes at once. Basil's week (a day a card, each meal a swap) used to be gathered at the end as 3 quick questions under one Send, so a swap never went. A lesson's quiz has no title and still waits for the end. Second, a reply with words for the chat that also redraws a named page (This week, Groceries) keeps you on the answer; the redraw keeps the page current, like a patch. The same redraw on its own still brings its page forward. A page the agent saved is a standing page, so its buttons are tools, not questions waiting on you. Both rules are in the spec (YL.md section 5) with reference functions stageChunks, pageForward and standingPages. Try it at yuigui.com/playground?demo=week-deck: it plays the runtime's real reply; tap a meal on Monday and the swap goes on the wire log, then open His pages and send only the redraw. Tests: chunks 12 and pages 12 pass, on the runtime's reply word for word.

title: The study buddy's flow: a topic to a quiz
short: Ask the chat on yuigui.com to teach you something and Quill walks you through it: pick a topic, a short lesson with a picture a page, one question. Then a calculator to play with, and the cards go in your review.
body: Chris, Sep 27: "we need to tell them about each member of the crew and they all need to have a multistep flow that is associated with it." Quill is fifth, after Arnold, Basil, Gouda and Penny. His flow, study-quiz, starts with a topic: how vaccines work, how a ball flies or how money grows. Then how much you know; know the basics and he skips the first page. The lesson is short, one idea a page and a picture on each: the mRNA in its bubble, a throw split into two motions, coins that grow faster every year. Then one question. Get it wrong and the next page shows why, with its picture; get it right and he moves on. Last, when to quiz you again. One Send and a calculator comes up to play with: slide the throw's angle and watch the distance peak at 45, slide the half-life and watch the mRNA fade, slide the rate and watch $1,000 double. Three cards go in his review table, due when you said, and the quiz lands in his sessions, the same columns his app uses. On the site chat that answer needs no model turn. Along the way the site chat learned to draw math: formulas in the chat used to show as plain letters. Try it: open the chat and say teach me something and quiz me, or play it at /playground?demo=flow-study-quiz. Tests: the flow e2e takes all 28 of its edges in six runs (805 checks across every flow, 0 failed), four unit tests (the path per answer, the calc and cards per topic, only the flow's own words reach the reply, the chat's stage) and a live run of the chat on a phone with the real model.

title: The planner's flow: a busy week to a plan
short: Ask the chat on yuigui.com to plan a busy week and Penny walks you through it: what's on, what matters most, when you get things done. Then your week lands on a timeline by day with a checklist to keep.
body: Chris, Sep 27: "we need to tell them about each member of the crew and they all need to have a multistep flow that is associated with it." Penny is fourth, after Arnold, Basil and Gouda. Her flow, planner-week, starts with what's on this week: a work deadline, appointments, errands, bills, family time, workouts. Pick more than three and she says it's a full week and one thing goes first. Then what matters most; a deadline asks when it's due. Then when you get things done and how many things a day. Anything with a time (an appointment, family dinner, workouts at a set hour) asks about reminders; a week with nothing timed skips that. One Send and the week lands as a timeline by day with Edit order: what matters most first, never more a day than you picked, fixed times kept. Under it, a checklist to keep, what matters most at the top, and the rows go in her tasks and reminders tables, the same columns her app uses. On the site chat that answer needs no model turn, so the week always matches what you told her. Try it: open the chat and say help me plan my busy week, or play it at /playground?demo=flow-planner-week. Tests: the flow e2e takes all 12 of its edges in three runs (640 checks across every flow, 0 failed), five unit tests (the path per answer, the pace per day, fixed times, reminders only when asked, only the flow's own words reach the reply) and a live run of the chat on a phone with the real model.

title: The musician's flow: a vibe to a beat
short: Ask the chat on yuigui.com how Gouda makes a beat and he walks you through it: pick a vibe and a tempo, change one row, pick the chords under it, and the loop plays with the chords under it, kept in his sessions.
body: Chris, Sep 27: "we need to tell them about each member of the crew and they all need to have a multistep flow that is associated with it." Gouda is third, after Arnold and Basil. His flow, musician-jam, starts from a vibe: lo-fi, boom bap, house or rock. Each vibe shows its own beat as a page, row by row, backbone first: kick on 1 and 3, snare or clap on 2 and 4, then hats and one flavor row, every row a different drum. Each vibe has its own tempo range too, so a house beat never crawls. Then change one row (busier hats, an extra kick, a shaker on top, or leave it) and pick the chords under it: warm is the pop four, jazzy has sevenths, and moody asks for a minor key instead. Just drums skips the key. One Keep and the loop starts playing with the chords under it on big buttons, and the beat lands in his sessions table, the same columns his app uses to open a beat again. On the site chat that answer needs no model turn, so the loop is always the beat you picked. Try it: open the chat and say show me how Gouda makes a beat, or play it at /playground?demo=flow-musician-jam. Tests: the flow e2e takes all 19 of its edges in four runs (537 checks across every flow, 0 failed), five unit tests (every vibe and every row change keeps the backbone, the saved row, the chords, only the flow's own words reach the reply) and a live run of the chat on a phone with the real model.

title: Your study buddy teaches and quizzes
short: Say Teach me how vaccines work and Quill asks how much time you have and what you know. One Send and a short lesson opens, one idea a page, ending in a quiz. What you learn becomes cards he brings back on the right day.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "we should focus the next stories on getting the crew more tools up with detailed flows... i want the agents to have default screens." Quill is next after Arnold, Basil, Gouda and Penny. Learn a topic (his shortcut, Teach me <topic>, or a subject on his first answer) is one full-screen flow: what happens first, then how much time you have and what you know already, one Send. Quill writes the lesson once and it opens on the stage as a deck, one idea a page with its key points or formula, ending in a graded quiz that shows why when you miss one. Finish it and your score lands on Progress. What the lesson taught becomes cards, first due tomorrow. Review my cards is one flow of the cards due today: think of the answer, see it, then tap Again, Hard, Good or Easy. Again brings a card back today, Hard tomorrow, Good and Easy further out each time, so the ones you know stop taking your time. What should I review next? is answered in one line. Walk me through a problem asks for the problem, then breaks it into steps, one a page, each with its own question; the next step only shows once you answer, so you do the thinking. His three screens stay current by themselves: What you're studying, Next review with the due count and Start, and Progress with your streak, cards reviewed this week, cards learned and your last quiz. The lesson and the steps are the only things that ask a model; the rest runs from his tables with no free turn. Tests: runtime 225 (13 new, on the real store path, a relaunch from saved data, every reply read by the Yui Lines parser, a real GLM lesson and problem checked by hand) and a live check on a throwaway account, 21 of 21. title: Your planner plans the week
short: Say Plan my week and talk it out: everything on your plate, in any order. Penny sorts it into days on a timeline you can drag, puts the next thing big on Today, and reminds you of anything with a time.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "we should focus the next stories on getting the crew more tools up with detailed flows... i want the agents to have default screens." Penny is next after Arnold, Basil and Gouda. Plan my week (her shortcut, the words, or the Plan button) is one full-screen flow: how it works first, then a big talk button for the brain dump (call the dentist tomorrow at 9, groceries, finish the report by Friday, pay the water bill, it's urgent), then the questions last: which days are already full, how many things a day, whether to bring in what's still open, and whether to remind you. One Send. She keeps the day and time you said, puts the urgent one first, and sorts the rest into the first days with room, never a full day and never more than you picked. It lands on This week, a timeline by day: tap Edit order and drag a task up, and it takes that place's day; or tap Move a task and pick a task and a day. Today shows the next thing big with a Done button, the list with ticks, and the evening review. What's next today? and Add a to-do: call mom tomorrow at 5 work in words too. A task with a time keeps a reminder, at the time or 10 minutes before, for the phone to ring in the app half. The evening review is two minutes: what got done, then each task still open, done, tomorrow or drop, and how the day went. One Send and tomorrow starts clean; the day is kept. title: Yui 0.5.2: the dots are back and slide with you
short: Build 288 brings back the small dots over the bar. Drag between an agent's screens and the screen follows your finger while the dot stretches and slides to the next one.
body: Chris, Sep 28: "put the navigation back ... the dots we removed, i also want those to slide, not fade between them and the dots should animate." His newer word wins over Sep 27's no dots. Now, when an agent has more than one screen, a small row of dots in its colors sits just above the bar. The one on show is a pill. Drag sideways and the screen moves with your finger, the next one coming in beside it, while the pill stretches toward the next dot and slides there, following the finger, not snapping at the end. Let go past a fifth of the screen, or flick, and it lands with a spring; less, and it springs back. Tap a dot to jump; that slides too. With Reduce Motion on, the screens cross-fade and the dots stay. It is still one sideways gesture from anywhere, the bars included, and keys, pads, maps and sliders keep their own drags. VoiceOver hears the dots as one control, "Screen 2, 2 of 4", and swipes up or down to page. Only the screen on show and the one beside it are drawn, so memory stays flat. title: Tables right in the reply, for any agent
short: A connected agent no longer needs a tool call to keep your tables. It writes table words in its reply, and your phone gets the screen with the real rows. Hermes, A2A and webhooks.
body: Chris: "this can be the UI layer no matter the AI agent you decide on." This morning a connected agent could keep your tables only through a tool call. Now it can just write table create, put and query in its reply, the same way Yui's own agents do. Before the reply is saved, the Hermes plugin, the A2A bridge and the webhook bridge hand it to Yui's one tables call. The rows land, the lines come out, and each query becomes a table, list, chart or number with the real rows. A reply of writes alone reads Saved. with the table that changed. A reply that only asks for rows is a read: nothing reaches your phone, the rows go back to the agent, and it answers you with them. Deletes still ask first: Delete or Keep, and a Hermes agent hears about your tap on its next turn. An A2A agent can also send a data part, and a webhook can return a tables field. After you hand a table to another agent, that agent's next turn opens with one line naming what it now holds, so it can carry on without the old agent. Only your own thread: a shared client's thread never touches your tables. Next: Controls > Tables in the app, with Give to... and when each table was last read. The page at /mockups/tables shows the live runs. Tests: runtime 159 of 159, Hermes plugin 10 new, A2A 61 of 61 offline and 81 of 81 live (A2A 1.0, 0.3 and poll), webhook 8 new offline tests in Python and Node, 28 of 28 live in each, and the Hermes reply path live at 17 of 17. Every live run used a throwaway account, deleted after.

title: Your tables work with any agent
short: A Hermes agent and a Claude agent over MCP now keep your tables on Yui's server. Hand a table from one to the other and it reads the same rows.
body: Chris: "this can be the UI layer no matter the AI agent you decide on." Yesterday only Yui's own agents kept tables on the server. Now any agent you connect does too. Hermes agents get a yui_tables tool in the Yui plugin, and Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client gets the same yui_tables tool on yui-mcp. Both land on one server call, on the same store and rules as native agents: table create, put, query, the same types, errors and limits. A table belongs to you and one agent holds it. Another agent asking for it hears No table called foods yet. You can give a table to another of your agents: it keeps its name and rows, the new agent reads it, the old one stops seeing it. Deletes still ask first: the agent's delete puts Delete or Keep in its thread, and only your tap removes anything. Every read is on the record. Limits: 50 lines a call, 100 tables a person, 60 calls a minute an agent. Next: table lines inside a connected agent's reply, A2A and webhook, and Give to... in Controls. title: One agent opens another
short: Ask Yui something that is Basil's job: Yui passes you over with a note, and Basil is already answering.
body: Chris, from TestFlight: "An agent should be able to call a method to open another agent." Now it can, with one line. Yui answers a food question with a card for Basil that says why: she just finished leg day and wants dinner ideas. A second and a half later the app is in Basil's thread, and Basil has already answered the note, with dinner options and a pick for the recipe. The card stays in Yui's thread, so a tap on Open Basil goes there again later; old messages never jump. Native agents get it on the server today. Hermes agents send the same card, and Yui tells the agent it names the way an @mention does; the guide teaches it when the build that jumps is on TestFlight. Native agents also answer in group threads now, each group with its own history, and reach connected agents with an @handle. Those agents only read what was written, never a native agent's notes or tables. One hand-off a reply, and an agent that was handed the person never passes them on again. Tests: the native runtime (140), the Hermes plugin suites, and the hand-off in the simulator in light and dark.

title: Log a meal without weighing
short: Send Basil a photo and a few words. He answers at once, works out the macros behind the scenes, then posts one breakdown and remembers each food.
body: Chris, on build 244: "I don't wanna make the user weigh that much... It should go as a separate task in a queue, analyze behind the scenes, and then update your screens when ready." And: "a full breakdown of all the calories and all the macros, and I don't need eight screens for that." Now a photo to Basil, with or without words, gets "Got it, working out the macros." in about two seconds. It used to sit on Thinking for 14. The meal goes into a queue on Yui's server. The model that sees names each item with a portion in plain words, never grams, and the runtime does the sums. Then one reply: a line with the total and how sure it is, a table of every item with calories, protein, carbs and fat, today so far and one donut chart. Basil asks at most one question, only when it moves the total by about 100 kcal, and never about what you already said. The tap is applied at once. Each food lands in your food memory with its numbers per portion, so your usual oatmeal is your oatmeal next time. A meal in words (two eggs and toast for breakfast) is logged the same way. No app build needed: it runs on the server for every Basil. Tests: the native runtime (133), a live eval of three meal photos with and without spoken notes (two tablespoons of butter adds 23 g of fat), and runs in the simulator on throwaway accounts in light and dark, deleted after.

images.alt: Basil's thread: a photo of grilled salmon with salad, the words lunch, cooked in a little butter, and Basil's answer at once: Got it, working out the macros.
The breakdown: a table of salmon, butter, avocado, lettuce, tomato and sauce with calories, protein, carbs and fat and a total of 504 kcal, today so far, and a donut of today's macros.
A meal said in words: Breakfast, two eggs and toast with butter, as a table with a total of 327 kcal and today's macros as a donut.

title: Meet each agent when you open it
short: Open an agent for the first time and it says hello on the full screen. The picker says what each one does, and About lists three things to ask it.
body: Chris, on build 244: "Arnold actually had a pretty decent little kickoff that he was about to do, but when I got to his screen for the first time, all it showed me was a blank screen." Now the first time you open an agent, its hello plays on the stage: Arnold's opening line, then his three questions on one screen with one Send. After that the agent opens the way it always has. The picker at the top is the only one now ("I like where you have the agent picker in the main. I think we can get rid of the agent picker from the left side bar"). Each agent in it has a short line under its name saying what it does, and Add an agent moved there too. In the drawer, About starts with that line, two sentences on what the agent does and three things to ask it. Tap one and it goes as your message. Where it runs moved lower and got quieter. Tests: new UI tests in light and dark (the hello plays once, the drawer has no picker, an About row sends), unit tests for the hello and the new fields, and the old drawer tests moved over to the top picker. Reaches phones with the next TestFlight build.

title: Switch agents, keep your tables
short: Your tables belong to you, not to one agent. Hand Basil's Foods table to a Claude agent and the same question draws the same screen.
body: Chris: "this can be the UI layer no matter the AI agent you decide on." Yesterday's native agents got their own tables on Yui's server (YUI-170). This is the plan for every other agent. A Hermes agent, a Claude or ChatGPT agent over MCP, an A2A agent and a webhook script all reach the same tables through one call on the relay, with the same three words: table create, put and query. Hermes and MCP get a yui_tables tool, A2A sends a data part, a webhook returns a tables field, and table lines in any reply work on every host. You own each table and one agent holds it at a time. Switch agents and Give to... moves it: same name, same rows, same screens, and the old agent stops seeing it. Removing an agent now asks if you want to keep its tables. The spec is section 8 of Agent tables, and the mock at /mockups/tables lets you hand Basil's Foods table to Chef on Claude and watch the call each host makes. Step 2 builds the adapters in the app repo. Tests: the site's YL and chat tests, a clean build, and a script that clicks through the mock in light and dark at 390 wide.
